actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository describes itself as 'MuJoCo models for Unitree Robots'
The card's main model is the MJCF scene a1.xml, whose root element is '<mujoco model="unitree_a1">'
The model uses radian angles (<compiler angle="radian"/>) and sets size njmax 500 and nconmax 100
The model header states that it is under the Apache License, Version 2.0
The torso body a1_torso has a free joint (<freejoint/>), so the model has a floating base
The robot has 12 hinge joints, three per leg (hip, thigh and calf): FR_hip, FR_thigh, FR_calf, then the same for FL, RR and RL
The joint ranges are hip -0.802851 to 0.802851, thigh -1.0472 to 4.18879 and calf -2.69653 to -0.916298
The model has 12 position actuators, one per hinge joint, with kp 60 on hip and thigh and kp 93.3 on calf
Every actuator sets ctrlrange to its joint range
The unitree default class sets ctrllimited true for position actuators
basic_scene.xml defines a ground plane geom of size 5 5 10
The five mesh assets are STL files under meshes/a1
The repository also contains aliengo.xml, whose root is '<mujoco model="unitree_aliengo">'
The repository also contains laikago.xml, whose root is '<mujoco model="unitree_laikago">'

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one model deterministically from one initial state; the bridge's reset restores the model defaults and takes no seed, so a run repeats exactly on the same engine but no seed selects a different start state

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the model file for the actuator control ranges, the joint dimensions and the free-joint start pose, but it integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated hinge and resolves no contact, actuator, equality or tendon dynamics
the free base is not integrated by the stand-in: gravity, the ground plane and contacts do not move it
no mesh or texture of meshes/a1 is loaded and no contact geometry is resolved
the model sets no <option timestep>, so the stand-in uses MuJoCo's library default 2 ms as a placeholder; a real MuJoCo load would use that same default
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine
the package serves the card's models[0] a1.xml only; aliengo.xml and laikago.xml are not served
no physical Unitree A1 is modelled and nothing was validated against the hardware

safe_state.description: the simulation holds its state: after an e-stop no step or reset runs until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the last integration state stays readable
